utterance: That does sound very much like a bladder infection. Before I confirm that, I need to check a few important things. First, to make sure it hasn't spread up towards your kidneys: have you had any fever or shivers, any pain in your back or side up under your ribs, or any nausea or vomiting?
reply: No fevers or shivers, and I haven’t been sick. No pain in my back or sides — just a bit of a tummy ache low down. I’m eating normally.

utterance: Good — that's reassuring. Now a few questions about other possible causes: have you noticed any unusual vaginal discharge, itching, or pain during sex? And are you sexually active at the moment — if so, has there been a new partner in the last few months? I ask because some sexually transmissible infections can cause similar burning, and I'd want to test for those as well if there's any chance.
reply: No, I haven't noticed any unusual discharge, itching, or pain during sex. I'm sexually active — I've been with the same boyfriend for about a year, just him.

utterance: Okay. You mentioned this feels like your last UTI — how many of these have you had before, and roughly when? Do you remember what antibiotic you were given and whether it cleared up completely?

utterance: Here's the plan, Chloe. You're taking one 300 mg tablet once a day for three days — please finish the whole course even if you feel better after a day or two. Most people notice a big improvement within 24 to 48 hours. In the meantime, drink plenty of water, and you can take paracetamol or ibuprofen from the pharmacy for the discomfort. A sachet of a urinary alkaliniser such as Ural, dissolved in water, can also ease the stinging while the antibiotic kicks in. A small number of people get nausea or a rash with this antibiotic — if you get a rash, stop taking it and let us know straight away.
reply: Thanks, that sounds doable. I'll make sure to finish the course and drink plenty of water. I'll take the paracetamol if it gets too sore.

utterance: Now the important part — when to come back or seek help urgently. If you develop a fever or shivers, pain in your back or side, vomiting, or you feel really unwell, that could mean the infection is travelling up to your kidneys, and you need to be seen urgently — come back here or go to the emergency department if it's after hours. Also come back if you're not clearly improving within 48 hours, if symptoms are still there after you finish the tablets, or if it comes back soon after — in that case we'd send your urine to the lab to check exactly which germ it is and which antibiotic works best. One last thing while you're here: the pill protects you from pregnancy but not from sexually transmissible infections, so condoms are still worth considering, and we're always happy to do a quick screening test if you'd ever like one. Any questions for me?
reply: No questions, thanks. I'll keep an eye on it and come back if things don't get better.

awards.label: Defensible diagnosis: Lower urinary tract infection
Reasonable differential: Urethritis from a sexually transmitted infection
